newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to count endangered Javan rhinos.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to count endangered Javan rhinos.

text.p: Indonesian environmentalists will hold a week-long census this month to determine the number of endangered Javan rhinoceroses still roaming the Ujung Kulon National Park in West Java.
The census will start on April 20 and is jointly organised by the management of the national park and environmentalists from the Indonesia office of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF).

"The census will last for a week and we will determine the number of the remaining Javan rhinos by counting the footprints," Nazir Fuad, a project officer for WWF's Ujung Kulon project, told Reuters on Monday.
Fuad said the last census two years ago estimated there were 50 to 60 rhinoceroses in the 120,000-hectare (296,520 acres) Ujung Kulon park, located on the westernmost tip of Java island.
He said a census was held every two years.
Conservationists said until the 18th century the single-horned rhinos could be found throughout Java.
But they were so numerous that the then Dutch colonial rulers paid money to have them killed. Five hundred were killed within two years in 18th century.

Fuad said poaching was not a threat anymore for the Javan rhinos because the government had imposed a strict law in which a poacher could be sentenced to up to 10 years in jail for illegal trading in wildlife, including rhinoceroses.
